name: open
synopsis: int open(const char *pathname, int flags, ... /*mode_t mode*/);
int openat(int dirfd, const char *pathname, int flags, ... /*mode_t mode*/);
int openat2(int dirfd, const char *pathname, const struct open_how *how, size_t size);
description: The open() system call opens the file specified by pathname and returns a file descriptor for subsequent operations. If the file does not exist and O_CREAT is specified in flags, it creates the file with the given mode.

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.description: The pathname of the file to open or create.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags specifying access mode (e.g., O_RDONLY, O_WRONLY, O_RDWR) and other options (e.g., O_CREAT, O_TRUNC).

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: File permission mode for creation, used if O_CREAT is specified.

return_value.success: Returns a new file descriptor (a nonnegative integer)
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: The requested access to the file is not allowed, or search permission is denied for a directory in the path, or write access to the parent directory is not allowed for creation.
For openat(), pathname is relative and dirfd is neither AT_FDCWD nor a valid file descriptor.
O_EXCL was specified and pathname refers to a block device in use by the system.
O_CREAT is specified, the file does not exist, and the user's quota of disk blocks or inodes is exhausted.
pathname already exists and O_CREAT and O_EXCL were used.
pathname points outside the accessible address space.
See EOVERFLOW.
Interrupted by a signal while waiting for a slow device.
Invalid value in flags, or O_TMPFILE without O_WRONLY or O_RDWR, or other invalid flag combinations.
pathname refers to a directory and write access was requested.
Too many symbolic links encountered in resolving pathname.
The per-process limit on open file descriptors has been reached.
pathname is too long.
The system-wide limit on open files has been reached.
pathname refers to a device special file with no corresponding device.
O_CREAT is not set and the file does not exist, or a directory component does not exist.
Insufficient kernel memory was available.
No space left on the device for creating the file.
A component in pathname is not a directory.
O_NONBLOCK and O_WRONLY are set for a FIFO with no reader, or the file is a device with no corresponding device.
The filesystem does not support O_TMPFILE.
pathname refers to a file too large to open.
The operation was prevented by a file seal or O_NOATIME without permission.
pathname is on a read-only filesystem and write access was requested.
pathname refers to an executable in use, a swap file with O_TRUNC, or a file being read by the kernel.
O_NONBLOCK was specified and an incompatible lease is held on the file.

examples: fd = open("/path/to/dir", O_TMPFILE | O_RDWR, S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR);
